notes: This file IS the module catalog. Adding a block means dropping a .sol next
to it and adding an entry here — no Rust change, no frontend change.
Arg tokens resolved by the deployment planner (graph.rs):
$param:<name>   a value the user typed into the inspector
$input:<portId> the address of the block wired to that input port
$self           the address of this block instance
$zero           the null address (an optional slot a wire fills later)
a|b             first token that resolves wins (used for optional ports)

blocks.name: Token
blocks.summary: ERC20 with an optional owner mint.
blocks.docs: The starting point for most compositions. Mints its initial supply to the deployer; leave `mintable` off for a fixed-supply asset.

params.name: initialSupply
params.label: Initial supply
params.help: Whole tokens, scaled by the decimals above.

blocks.name: Yield Vault
blocks.summary: ERC4626-shaped vault. Issues shares, optionally routes to a strategy.
blocks.docs: Deposits mint shares priced off totalAssets(), so any yield the strategy reports accrues to holders. The share token is itself an erc20 output — wire it into staking or an AMM.

blocks.name: Fixed-Yield Strategy
blocks.summary: Pays a fixed APR on deposited principal, out of a funded reserve.
blocks.docs: Only recognises yield the reserve can actually cover, so a composed protocol never reports assets it cannot pay out. Fund it with fund(amount).

blocks.name: Staking Rewards
blocks.summary: Stake one token, earn another at a per-second rate.
blocks.docs: Classic accRewardPerShare accounting. Point the stake port at an AMM's LP token for liquidity mining, or at a vault share for boosted yield.

blocks.name: AMM Pair
blocks.summary: Constant-product pair with LP shares and a fee.
blocks.docs: x*y=k with a bps fee to LPs. Exposes price() so it can also satisfy an oracle port — convenient on a testnet, but a spot AMM price is manipulable, so prefer a dedicated feed for anything liquidatable.

blocks.name: Lending Pool
blocks.summary: Borrow one asset against another at an oracle-priced LTV.
blocks.docs: Single collateral, single debt asset, linear borrow interest, liquidation at a health factor below 1. Needs an oracle port — that is the wire that makes it a real market.

blocks.name: Price Feed
blocks.summary: Owner-published price, 1e18 scaled, with a staleness guard.
blocks.docs: Reverts on reads older than maxStaleness so a stalled feed fails closed instead of quietly liquidating people at the wrong price. Set maxStaleness to 0 to disable.

blocks.name: Fee Splitter
blocks.summary: Splits an ERC20 balance between two payees by basis points.
blocks.docs: Make the revenue split part of the diagram. Shares must sum to 10000.

blocks.name: BlocTime Treasury
blocks.summary: Locks a position and pays it out weekly, pro-rata by BlocTime weight.
blocks.docs: What you lock here you cannot take back early. Every Friday 12:00 EST — the same instant BlocTime sweeps its own pot — anyone may call distribute(), and the week's payout is split across the registered holders in proportion to their BLOC. A lock either streams its principal out in equal weekly slices (returnPrincipal off) or sits escrowed for its term while only the yield on top is shared (returnPrincipal on). Wire the asset port to the token the position pays in, or paste its address; leave the weight port unwired to use the live BlocTime deployment. Holders must register() to be eligible — this contract reads the BLOC token from outside and cannot checkpoint transfers, so an open accumulator would pay whoever bought BLOC after the fact.

params.name: assetToken
params.label: Asset address
params.help: Only used when the asset port is left unwired. The token the chosen position pays in — a stablecoin, a vault share. Deployment reverts on the zero address.

params.name: weightToken
params.label: BlocTime (BLOC) address
params.help: The BlocTime deployment whose BLOC balances decide the split. Defaults to the fleet's Base Sepolia instance; point it at your own fork's BlocTime to use those weights.

blocks.name: Timelock
blocks.summary: Queue-then-execute delay. Outputs a governor address.
blocks.docs: Wire its governor output into any block's Owner port and every privileged call on that block has to wait out the delay in public first.

blocks.name: Vesting
blocks.summary: Linear vesting with a cliff, optionally revocable.
blocks.docs: Fund it by transferring tokens in; vested() tracks whatever the contract holds plus what has already been released.

blocks.name: Faucet
blocks.summary: Rate-limited drip of a test token.
blocks.docs: Transfer tokens in to fill it. Every testnet composition wants one; this one at least has a cooldown.

blocks.name: CDP Stablecoin
blocks.summary: Lock collateral, mint a stablecoin against it, pay a stability fee.
blocks.docs: The MakerDAO shape. The block IS the stablecoin, so the unit it issues is an erc20 output you can wire into a PSM, a savings rate or a pool. Positions are liquidatable below the collateral ratio, and stability fees accumulate as protocol surplus that drawSurplus() mints to the revenue sink.

params.name: minCollateralRatioBps_
params.label: Min collateral ratio (bps)
params.help: 15000 = 150%. Below this a position can be liquidated.

blocks.name: Peg Stability Module
blocks.summary: Swap a reserve asset for the protocol stablecoin at par, minus a fee.
blocks.docs: Maker's PSM. It is what turns a stablecoin that exists into a stablecoin that holds — arbitrage against a par window in both directions. It swaps out of inventory rather than minting, so fill whichever side you want to defend. Decimals are read from both tokens, so a 6-decimal reserve against an 18-decimal unit is handled.

params.name: gemDecimals
params.label: Reserve decimals
params.help: Only used to scale the cap you type. USDC is 6, most protocol units are 18.

blocks.name: Savings Rate
blocks.summary: Deposit the unit, hold a share that grows at a governance-set rate.
blocks.docs: The DSR / sDAI shape. Yield is an accrual index, never a rebase, so the share token composes as an ordinary erc20 downstream. Interest is only payable out of the buffer someone funded — read shortfall() to see whether the rate is promised or backed.

blocks.name: StableSwap Pool
blocks.summary: Curve's invariant for assets that should trade at par. Amplified, low fee.
blocks.docs: Between a constant sum and a constant product, leaning on the first while the pool is balanced. Use it wherever a constant-product pair would charge curvature for nothing: a stablecoin against its reserve, an LST against the asset it wraps. Exposes virtualPrice() for LP accounting and price() as an oracle output.

params.name: amp_
params.label: Amplification (A)
params.help: Higher A = flatter curve near par. Curve's 3pool runs around 2000; a volatile pair wants single digits.

blocks.name: Liquid Staking
blocks.summary: Deposit an asset, hold a liquid share while it earns; rewards are reported in.
blocks.docs: The Lido shape, share-priced rather than rebasing — a rebase breaks every integration that stored a number. An operator stakes the buffer out and reports rewards, which must arrive as real tokens; the protocol fee is taken in newly minted shares, diluting holders by exactly the fee. Exits go through an unbonding queue, because real staking cannot exit instantly.

blocks.name: Vote-Escrow Lock
blocks.summary: Lock a token for up to four years for a weight that decays to zero.
blocks.docs: veCRV. Weight is amount × time remaining, so power costs time instead of capital you can borrow for one block. The weight reads like an erc20 but every transfer path reverts — which is exactly what makes it safe as a vote token for a governor with no snapshots, and as the boost source for a gauge.

params.name: maxLock_
params.label: Max lock (seconds)
params.help: 126144000 is four years — the veCRV maximum, and the cap this block enforces.

blocks.name: Boosted Gauge
blocks.summary: Emissions on a staked LP token, boosted up to 2.5× by vote-escrow weight.
blocks.docs: The second half of the Curve design. Your working balance is 40% of your deposit plus 60% weighted by your share of total ve, capped at your deposit — so the maximum boost is 2.5×. With no escrow wired it degrades to plain staking, everyone at 1×. Anyone can kick() a wallet whose lock expired.

blocks.name: Perp Market
blocks.summary: Levered longs and shorts against an oracle, with an LP pool as counterparty.
blocks.docs: The GMX shape. Traders post margin and take a levered position; liquidity providers mint an LP share and are the other side of every one. Funding is skew-based — the crowded side pays — and positions below maintenance margin can be closed by anyone for a keeper fee. The LP share is an erc20 output: stake it, pair it, vault it.

params.name: maxLeverageBps_
params.label: Max leverage (bps)
params.help: 50000 = 5×. The contract caps this at 50× regardless.

blocks.name: Bond Depository
blocks.summary: Sell the protocol token at a discount for reserves, vested over a term.
blocks.docs: OlympusDAO's answer to renting liquidity. Price comes off the wired oracle — point it at the pair the token trades on and the bond re-prices every block — and the discount narrows as debt approaches the ceiling, which is the loop that stops one dip from draining the treasury. Reserves go straight through to the treasury sink.

blocks.name: Flash Lender
blocks.summary: ERC-3156 flash loans out of a depositor-owned reserve.
blocks.docs: Borrow the whole reserve for one call as long as it returns with the fee inside the same transaction. Deposits mint a share whose value grows with fees, so the reserve is itself a yield-bearing erc20 — and a protocol share of the fee can be routed to a sink.

blocks.name: Governor
blocks.summary: Propose, vote, execute. Outputs an owner port every block can obey.
blocks.docs: Governor Bravo without the indexer. Votes are the caller's balance at the moment they vote rather than a historical checkpoint — which is why the natural vote token here is a vote-escrow lock, a weight nobody can borrow for one block. Wire a timelock and the deployment hands it the admin key, so passed proposals execute through the delay.

wires.note: timelock takes orders from the governor

blocks.name: Safety Module
blocks.summary: Stake to backstop the protocol: emissions to wait, a cooldown to leave, slashable.
blocks.docs: Aave's stkAAVE. The cooldown is the point — insurance you can withdraw the instant it is needed is not insurance — so exiting is signal, wait, then leave inside a short window. A slash is capped and moves the exchange rate rather than any one balance, so the loss lands on everyone in proportion.

blocks.name: Merkle Airdrop
blocks.summary: One root, thousands of claimants, each paying their own gas.
blocks.docs: The Uniswap distributor. Publish a root, let holders prove membership, sweep what nobody claimed when the window closes. Claims are one bit each, 256 to a storage slot. The root can still be replaced right up until the first claim lands.

params.name: merkleRoot_
params.label: Merkle root
params.help: Set it later with setRoot() if the list is not final at deploy time.

templates.name: Vault + Strategy
templates.summary: A token, a yield vault over it, and a fixed-rate strategy behind the vault.

templates.name: AMM + Liquidity Mining
templates.summary: Two tokens, a pair, and a staking block paying rewards on the LP token.

templates.name: Governed Money Market
templates.summary: Collateral + debt asset + price feed into a lending pool, all owned by a timelock.

templates.name: Yield → BlocTime Treasury
templates.summary: A token, a vault farming a fixed rate over it, and a treasury that locks the yield and pays it out weekly to BLOC holders.
